title: Geolocation
description: Origin and destination cells under a DECLARED geocode standard — where an order originates and terminates, at the grain of a neighborhood. Composed for ANY modality and BOTH physical and digital value chains. The standard is one of the cell grids whose grain the clause engines cap: geohash (6 characters at most), H3 (resolution 8 at most), S2 (level 13 at most) or Open Location Code (code length 6 at most). The standard is the source of truth — referenced, never restated. A clause that needs another standard, a jurisdiction code among them, is a clause of its own. Carries no physical-shipment assumption; mass and volume live in the elective figaro-cargo clause.

fields.name: geocodeStandard
fields.label: Geocode standard
fields.description: How the two location codes below are written: geohash (the default), H3, S2 or Open Location Code. These are the standards whose grain the clause engines read, so each public code is held to the neighborhood.

fields.name: geocoder
fields.label: Geocoder
fields.description: A Nominatim-compatible geocoding endpoint the parties resolve typed locations through when producing the origin/destination codes — a DESIGN fill: the designer pins it when tailoring the assembly, so every party to the trade resolves through the SAME service instead of whatever each client happened to configure. Optional: a party may produce the codes without one. An OPEN axis: any https endpoint speaking the declared standard's resolution is valid.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: Where the order starts, as a location code in the standard above. Give the neighborhood, never the door: a geohash of six characters or fewer, an H3 cell of resolution 8 or coarser, an S2 cell of level 13 or coarser, or an Open Location Code of length 6 or less. The exact address travels privately to the other party at hand-off; it is never written to the chain.
fields.label: Origin

fields.name: destination
fields.description: Where the order ends, as a location code in the standard above. Your phone can fill it from its location. Give the neighborhood, never the door: a geohash of six characters or fewer, an H3 cell of resolution 8 or coarser, an S2 cell of level 13 or coarser, or an Open Location Code of length 6 or less. The exact address travels privately to the other party at hand-off; it is never written to the chain.
